1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The time budget. The routine for every task. Using the documentation well. Domain checklists. Common traps. The final week.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: the commands in this module were used in the executed labs of Modules zero to thirteen (Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero).

1.title: The time budget
1.text: The time budget. The figure shows this: The time budget. Exam tip: Plan about six to eight minutes per task, easy tasks first, and keep about ten minutes to verify.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. The exam is two hours for fifteen to twenty tasks. That is an average of six to eight minutes per task, with the passing score at sixty-six percent. Points differ per task (the exact points per task are not published on the pages used for this course), so.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. Spend the first two minutes skimming the whole list if the interface allows; otherwise start in order. find the quick wins early. Do easy tasks first, flag hard ones. one fifteen-minute task can cost two easy ones. If you are stuck after about six minutes, flag it and move on. partial progress on many tasks beats perfection on few. Keep ten minutes at the end to re-verify. a typo in a namespace costs a full task. Do not leave a task half-broken (a half-edited manifest). the checker sees the final state. Where the points are (by domain weight): Troubleshooting thirty percent, Architecture twenty-five percent, Networking twenty percent, Workloads fifteen percent, Storage ten percent. Storage tasks are few and usually quick; Troubleshooting tasks are many and vary in length.

1.title: The routine for every task
1.text: The routine for every task. Read the whole task, including the last line (names, namespaces, "do not change..."). Run the context line ( kube control config use context... ). Check with kube control config current context. Note exact names, namespaces, ports, labels, file paths. Copy them from the task text, never retype from memory. Do it with the fastest tool (imperative command, the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, kube control explain, one docs page). Verify with a different command from the one that created it (create with kube control create, verify with kube control get dash o wide or describe slash a test Pod). Move on. Exam tip: Verify each task with a second command before you move on.

1.title: Using the documentation well
1.text: Using the documentation well. You may use Kubernetes dot I O or docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs and gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io (C K A only), the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under slash usr slash share. You may use the Kubernetes dot I O search; you must not open results from outside the allowed sites. Learn where things are before the exam: Concepts for explanations, Tasks for step-by-step yamel (R back, P V (Persistent Volume) slash P V C (Persistent Volume Claim), probes, Network Policy, E T C D backup under "Administer a Cluster", Ingress, Gateway A P I), Reference for kube control cheat sheet and kube A D M commands. Prefer kube control explain for field names (faster than the browser). Copy examples, then change names; do not retype a long yamel. Browser tabs and the terminal share the screen; practice with only the allowed pages.

1.title: Domain checklists
1.text: Domain checklists. Troubleshooting (thirty percent): get, describe, logs the previous flag, get events the sort by flag set to dot last Timestamp; nodes: system control, journal control dash u kubelet; control plane: C R I C T L ps dash a, C R I C T L logs, manifests in slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests; services: selector, endpoints, target Port, D N S, Network Policy; kube control top. Cluster Architecture (twenty-five percent): R back ( create role slash rolebinding... the verb flag the resource flag, auth can i ), kube A D M ( token create the print join command flag, certs check expiration, upgrade order), E T C D ( snapshot save with endpoint and three cert flags, E T C D U T L snapshot restore, edit the data-dir path in the manifest, restart control plane components), Helm ( install slash upgrade slash rollback slash template ), Kustomize ( apply dash k ), C R Ds (Custom Resource Definitions), drain or cordon.

1.title: Domain checklists, continued
1.text: Domain checklists. Services and Networking (twenty percent): Services ( expose, types, ports), D N S names, Ingress (class, host or path, path Type ), Gateway A P I (Gateway Class, Gateway, H T T P Route), Network Policy (and versus or, D N S for egress), Core D N S. Workloads and Scheduling (fifteen percent): rollouts ( set image, rollout undo ), Config Map or Secret, probes, resources, Limit Range or Resource Quota, labels or selectors or affinity or taints, Daemon Set or Stateful Set or Job, H P A (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler). Storage (ten percent): P V or P V C binding rules, Storage Class default and reclaim policy, access modes, Wait For First Consumer.

1.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)
1.text: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab). Wrong cluster context. run and verify the context line. Wrong namespace (object created in default ). dash n on every command, or set the context namespace; verify with get dash A then pipe to grep name. Resource created but misspelled name. copy names from the task. Pod fields immutable. delete and recreate ( the force flag the grace period flag zero ). Cluster Role plus Role Binding scope. Role Binding equals one namespace. role Ref immutable. delete and recreate the binding. Network Policy blocks D N S. allow U D P or T C P fifty-three in egress. Selector typo equals no endpoints. get endpointslices, the show labels flag. Edited a static Pod manifest wrongly. back up first, then C R I C T L logs. Exam tip: Check the first three traps on every task: the wrong context, the wrong namespace and a misspelled name; copy names from the task.

1.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab), continued
1.text: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab). E T C D restore without pointing the Pod at the new directory. edit the host path in the E T C D manifest. Forgot to restart control plane components after an E T C D restore. restart A P I server, controller manager, scheduler. Used a toleration and expected placement. combine with node selector slash affinity. Left a typo-free but unverified answer. verify every task. Rebooted base or used the Insert key. not allowed.

1.title: The final week
1.text: The final week. Redo the break-and-fix labs (Troubleshooting is thirty percent) until you can do each in under six minutes. Run the two timed mixed sets (Modules fourteen and fifteen) under exam conditions: two hours, only the allowed documentation. Use the killer dot S H simulator that comes with the exam registration (two attempts of thirty-six hours each): it is the closest to the real environment, including the S S H node workflow this course imitates with docker exec. Practice the speed kit (Module zero) until k, do and kube control explain are automatic. Re-read the Quick Reference Cards of every module. Check the current curriculum version and exam page before booking: the exam moves to a new Kubernetes version every few months; rules, fees and allowed resources can change.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How much time per task do you have on average? Answer: About six to eight minutes (two hours for fifteen to twenty tasks). Question two. What should you do after about six minutes on a stuck task? Answer: Flag it and move on; return at the end. Question three. What is the first thing you do in each task? Answer: Run the context line and note exact names and namespaces.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name two fast ways to avoid hand-writing yamel. Answer: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml and copying examples from the documentation. Question five. Which tool beats the browser for field names? Answer: kube control explain. Question six. What is the passing score? Answer: sixty-six percent.

1.title: Recall Check 3
1.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. After an E T C D restore, what must you do besides pointing the E T C D Pod at the new data directory? Answer: Restart the A P I server, controller manager and scheduler so they drop stale caches. Question eight. Which simulator is included with the exam registration? Answer: killer dot S H (two attempts of thirty-six hours each).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Time: two hours, fifteen to twenty tasks, about six to eight minutes each, sixty-six percent to pass. Order: easy first, flag hard, ten minutes to verify. Every task: context line, exact names, verify with a second command. Docs: Kubernetes dot I O, helm dot S H, gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io only. Weights: T thirty, A twenty-five, N twenty, W fifteen, S ten. Practice: break-and-fix labs, timed sets, killer dot S H. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
